business_scope.primary_industry_name: Virtual Performance Hosting and Digital Ticket Tokenization

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Luxembourg (unitary national jurisdiction; no sub-state fiscal distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Romano-Germanic), unified at national level; corporate and partnership law governed by the Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended; SCSp (Société en Commandite Spéciale) regime introduced by the Law of 12 July 2013 and adapted from Anglo-American limited partnership concepts; EU regulations directly applicable
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (freedom of establishment and services)
OECD Multilateral Convention to Implement Tax Treaty Related Measures to Prevent BEPS (MLI)
Belgium-Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU) - China Bilateral Investment Treaty (signed 2005, in force 2009)
Luxembourg - China Double Taxation Agreement (signed 14 March 1994, in force; as supplemented by exchange of notes)
Luxembourg - Hong Kong SAR Double Taxation Agreement (signed 2007, in force)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended (AML/CFT Law); CSSF Regulation No 12-02 of 14 December 2012, as amended (AML/CFT procedures); Law of 13 January 2019 instituting the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), as amended by the Law of 21 July 2020 (transposing AMLD5) and restricted in alignment with CJEU Judgment of 22 November 2022, Joined Cases C-37/20 and C-601/20; Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies and the Luxembourg Business Registers; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 22 December 2017 on further AML/CFT obligations; EU Council Regulations on restrictive measures (sanctions) directly applicable in Luxembourg as enforced by the Luxembourg Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (RBE is accessible to Luxembourg competent authorities, AML/CFT-obliged entities within customer due diligence procedures, and persons demonstrating a legitimate interest; no blanket public access since the CJEU ruling of 22 November 2022; SCSp, although lacking separate legal personality, is an RCS-registered entity and is subject to mandatory RBE declaration)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Limited partnership agreement (acte constitutif) of the SCSp, including the name, registered office, GP/LP capital commitments, profit-sharing and duration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg notary (Chambre des Notaires du Grand-Duché de Luxembourg); notarial execution is the prevailing professional standard and expedites RCS registration and banking acceptance
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarial deed executed in Luxembourg; no foreign legalization or apostille required for RCS filing

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing and Constitutional Documents of any foreign corporate general partner or limited partner entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry of the entity's country of origin (e.g., PRC SAMR registry or Hong Kong Companies Registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille Convention of 5 October 1961 (China acceded with effect from 7 November 2023; apostilles issued by PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs or authorized regional offices; consular legalization no longer required for Chinese public documents)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copies and proof of residential address of each managing partner, general partner, limited partner and ultimate beneficial owner (KYC/UBO pack)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed credit institution, notary, or certified professional in the country of issuance
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified true copy by a regulated professional; notarized and apostilled where the certifying professional is not within Luxembourg/EU regulated channels

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney for incorporation formalities, RCS filings and RBE declaration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Each founding partner and each beneficial owner (individual or corporate body)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized and apostilled if executed abroad (Hague Apostille Convention; PRC apostilles effective 7 November 2023); executed before a Luxembourg notary if signed in Luxembourg

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all general partners, limited partners, directors, and ultimate beneficial owners against the OFAC SDN List, UN Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and Luxembourg national asset-freezing designations; PEP assessment per FATF Recommendation 12 and CSSF Regulation No 12-02; risk-based enhanced due diligence required for PEPs, dual nationals of high-risk jurisdictions, and structures involving cryptocurrency payment rails; acceptance of USDC payments by the SCSp operating company is treated as normal trade receipts and does not in itself create a Virtual Asset Service Provider status, provided the entity does not provide exchange, custody, or third-party transfer services; any change in payment-rail scope requires re-profiling before launch; all screening results to be documented and retained for at least five years after termination of the business relationship under Article 5 of the AML/CFT Law.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_piercing_narrative: For the SCSp, UBO identification pierces through (i) the general partner (whether a corporate entity or individual) and (ii) each limited partner without exception until physical-person ownership or control is established; the 25% threshold applies to capital interests, voting rights, or control by other means; RBE disclosure covers name, nationality, date of birth, country of residence, nature and extent of beneficial interest; nominee and trust arrangements are disfavored and trigger mandatory suspicious-transaction reporting where concealment is suspected.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) at https://www.lbr.lu, hosting the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS); electronic filings and name verification conducted via MyGuichet (https://guichet.lu); official name availability search and RCS publication in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be written in Latin script; French, German, English, and Luxembourgish names are accepted; the mandatory statutory suffix 'SCSp' or the full phrase 'Société en commandite spéciale' must appear immediately before or after the selected name pursuant to Article 16-2 of the Law of 10 August 1915; the name must be distinctive, non-misleading, and not identical or confusingly similar to any name already registered in the RCS or to a protected trade name; non-Latin scripts are transliterated and a certified translation must be submitted with the notarial deed; names implying a regulated activity require prior authorization before reservation.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque / Bank / Banking (requires CSSF and European Central Bank authorization)
Assurance / Insurance / Réassurance (requires Commissariat aux Assurances authorization)
SICAV / SICAF / SIF / FCP / OPCVM / Investment Fund / Fonds (requires CSSF authorization as an undertaking for collective investment)
Fiduciaire / Trust / Trusteeship (requires Ministry of Justice authorization)
Réviseur d'entreprises / Audit / Expert-comptable / Comptable (regulated statutory-auditor or accountant professions)
Avocat / Law Firm / Legal (requires Luxembourg Bar admission if implying legal practice)
Bourse / Stock Exchange / Clearing / Settlement (regulated market infrastructure tokens)
Securities / Broker / Titres (implying MiFID investment services without authorization)
État / Gouvernement / Ministère / Luxembourg (as a token implying official state sponsorship or royal patronage)
University / Académie (misleading official or educational designation)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: In Luxembourg there is no statutory extension of an initial name reservation; a reservation lapses after 30 days and a fresh availability search and re-blocking must be made. Upon rejection by the RCS registrar on grounds of identical or confusing similarity, the applicant may (i) revise the proposed name and re-file through the notary; (ii) within one month of notification of the refusal, file an appeal before the commercial chamber of the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg (Luxembourg District Court) seeking reversal of the registrar's decision; (iii) if rejection arises from a sensitive or prohibited token, obtain the relevant prior ministerial or CSSF clearance and thereafter resubmit; provisional re-reservation of the corrected name may be made for a further 30-day window.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Partially permissible and strictly conditioned. An SCSp must maintain a registered office in Luxembourg; a commercial domiciliation provider authorized under the Law of 31 May 1999 may lawfully supply the registered-office address. However, a purely virtual 'letterbox' SCSp with no operational presence is unacceptable: the entity must evidence substantive decision-making, accounting records, bank account management, and administrative presence proportionate to its virtual-concert and digital-ticketing activity. For ISIC 7110 / NAICS 711310 operations, the SCSp must demonstrate that intellectual property, payment-processing contracts (Stripe, USDC), revenue recognition, and partner-level management decisions are rooted in Luxembourg; otherwise tax-residence and substance-challenge risk is materially elevated.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate, quantified at approximately 15% probability of an unannounced physical inspection within the first 24 months after incorporation; probability rises above 35% where the SCSp applies for a Luxembourg tax-residence certificate, registers for Luxembourg VAT, or engages in cross-border digital ticket tokenization with substantial third-party payment flows; inspections are typically conducted by the RCS registrar, Ministry of Justice, and tax administration in connection with substance- and AML-related audits.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Loi du 10 août 1915 sur les sociétés commerciales), notably Articles 29-33 and 943-1 to 943-24 governing the Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp); implementing Grand-Ducal Regulation of 23 July 2016; RCS operational guidelines.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), managed by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), 14-16 Boulevard Roosevelt, L-2450 Luxembourg; online filing via www.lbr.lu and the eFormalities portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acte de constitution / statuts (SCSp limited partnership agreement) and application for registration ('demande d'inscription au registre de commerce et des sociétés'), filed with the RCS and published in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital or legal escrow account for an SCSp. Contributions in cash, kind or labour are agreed contractually; a cash contribution is due and payable into the SCSp's bank account, while any deferred payment must be expressly accepted by the general partner in the partnership agreement.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporation documentation and form of SCSp partnership agreement be and are hereby approved in the form submitted to this meeting; the initial capital contribution schedule set out therein is adopted; the registered office is fixed at [address], Luxembourg; and the appointment of [Name] as manager and [Name] as compliance officer for the purpose of registering the SCSp with the Luxembourg Business Registers is confirmed; all filings, declarations, and payments necessary to obtain legal personality are authorized; and any officer or appointee is empowered to execute banking and tax registration forms as required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Availability Search and Preliminary Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, online search and reservation module at www.lbr.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Search the RCS index in the proposed corporate name to confirm it is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name and does not violate Luxembourg public policy. If required by the RCS, submit a name reservation request through the LBR online portal together with a draft extract of the partnership agreement and the confirmed registered office address.
required_dossiers: Full identity and address of the general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, add a distinctive element or alternative suffix and resubmit; appeal to the RCS registrar is available within 15 days under the Law of 10 August 1915.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of the SCSp Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: External Luxembourg law firm or notary public (notaire) acting on behalf of the founders
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the partnership agreement (statuts / contrat de société) in accordance with Articles 943-1 to 943-24 of the Law of 10 August 1915. The agreement must state the SCSp name, registered office, corporate object (virtual performance hosting and digital ticket tokenization), duration, initial capital or contribution schedule, classes of partnership interests, management and control powers, profit share and transfer rules. Execute the agreement by private signature unless a contribution comprises real estate, in which case a notarial deed is mandatory.
required_dossiers: Identity documents or corporate constitutional documents of each partner
Source of funds and proof of address for partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS later raises drafting objections, the partnership agreement must be amended by an addendum or, if notarial execution was initially excluded, a notarial instrument remedying the defect may be filed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening and Payment of Capital Contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution selected by the general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a partnership bank account in the SCSp's name and arrange for any cash contribution due under the partnership agreement to be transferred. Provide the bank with the signed partnership agreement, RCS name reservation confirmation, partner identity documents and source-of-wealth information. No escrow is required by law, but the bank may require a transitional blocked account before legal personality is obtained if mandated by internal AML policy.
required_dossiers: RCS name reservation certificate or confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses the account, provide additional economic rationale, adjust the AML/KYC details, or choose an alternate Luxembourg bank; the RCS registration does not depend on a bank certificate for an SCSp.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Registration Application with the RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), eFormalities portal at www.lbr.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the application for RCS registration, attaching the executed partnership agreement (private or notarial), the residential/registered office consent of the landlord, the declaration of appointment of the general partner's manager, and the statutory fee. Pay the RCS inscription duty online. The RCS will verify the legal form, name, registered office, object, and capacity of the signers.
required_dossiers: Registered office consent and lease/address proof
Identity documents and manager appointment declarations
Declaration of accuracy and legal compliance
UBO declaration under Luxembourg AML legislation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query or 'mise en demeure', correct the requested items and resubmit within the stated deadline; if registration is refused, a formal judicial appeal to the District Court of Luxembourg is available.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Legal Personality Confirmation and RESA Publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCS and the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once the RCS accepts the application, an RCS extract is issued and the publication in RESA occurs. Legal personality is acquired upon registration. Download the RCS certificate and identify all registration numbers and the national identification number of the SCSp.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication in RESA is delayed or incomplete, request written confirmation from LBR and, if necessary, issue a formal notification; the effective date of legal personality remains the RCS registration date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Tax, VAT and Social Security Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and direct tax; Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CNSS) if hiring employees
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the VAT and tax registration application with the AEDT using the RCS extraction, statutory partnership agreement, and manager identification; obtain a Luxembourg VAT number. If the SCSp employs staff, register with CNSS. As the SCSp is transparent, registration may also be required for income-tax purposes at the level of each partner according to their residence.
required_dossiers: Partnership agreement and corporate object description
Manager identification and proof of authority
Forecast of virtual event ticketing revenues
Payroll details, if any, for CNSS registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If AEDT questions the activity or business plan, submit an explanatory note on the virtual concert and digital ticketing model; for CNSS issues, provide stricter payroll schedules and dispute formal notices through the CNSS mediation procedure.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – no physical manufacturing plant or physical event venue. For any future physical promotional event, the competent body would be the Ministry of the Economy (Direction générale de l'industrie, PME) and the relevant communal authority for event permits.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industrial operating licence is required for a purely virtual concert and digital ticket tokenization platform; only a standard business registration under the Luxembourg RCS is required.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, du Climat et du Développement durable (MECDD) – Administration de l'environnement
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – the activity is a digital service without physical installations; no full EIA report or environmental authorization is required, unless the SCSp later controls data centre or physical hosting infrastructure subject to Luxembourg environmental law.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to virtual operations. If a cloud or data-centre partner is used, its own operations must comply with EU and Luxembourg standards on waste heat, energy consumption, WEEE (Directive 2012/19/EU) and general waste handling; no wastewater, VOC or flue-gas permit is required at the SCSp level.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No civil-defence or fire-safety permit is required for a virtual venue. If the SCSp leases administrative offices, the premises must satisfy the Labour Inspectorate (ITM) workplace occupational safety rules, including fire extinguishers, accessible exits, and electrical safety certifications. If the SCSp hosts live 3D/VR events, no additional clearance applies beyond ordinary office-compliant equipment shielding and GDPR-compliant data processing.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct income tax; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AED) for VAT; e-filing portal: MyGuichet.lu and Guichet.public.lu; customs: Administration des douanes et accises.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Upon incorporation of the SCSp with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS/LBR), the entity is automatically assigned a Luxembourg national identification number (matricule) which serves as the statutory TIN; for VAT, the SCSp or its foreign-entity owner must file a VAT registration application (Formulaire 105 - inscription à la TVA) with the AED through MyGuichet.lu, after which the AED issues a VAT identification number in the format LU + 8 digits; non-resident entities with no Luxembourg establishment that carry out taxable supplies may register directly for VAT or appoint an approved fiscal representative, in particular when the entity is established outside the EU.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not operate a US-style check-the-box election; the SCSp is statutorily fiscally transparent (tax transparent) by default under Luxembourg law, with each partner taxed personally on their distributable share; no domestic election exists to render the SCSp opaque, although the transposition of the EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive (ATAD) and the hybrid mismatch rules may reclassify the SCSp as opaque in Luxembourg where a foreign partner jurisdiction treats it as taxable, triggering DAC6 reportable arrangements and ATAD 2 counter-measures.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée - TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover (VAT franchise threshold under Article 148 of the Luxembourg VAT law); registration is mandatory once turnover exceeds EUR 35,000 or immediately for cross-border intra-Community acquisitions; B2C digital ticket sales to EU consumers are subject to OSS registration either in Luxembourg or in the EU member state of consumption.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time transaction-by-transaction fiscal clearance or digital stamping is in force; mandatory Peppol-compliant electronic invoicing applies exclusively to B2G supplies (public sector procurement under Directive 2014/55/EU); B2B and B2C e-invoicing is voluntary, subject to customer acceptance; VAT returns and recapitulative statements (DEB/EC Sales List) are filed electronically with the AED, and Standard Audit File for Tax (SAF-T) reporting is due only upon express AED demand during an audit.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supplies of goods physically dispatched or transported outside the EU qualify for the 0% export rate under Article 53(1) of the Luxembourg VAT law, provided definitive export is evidenced within a reasonable period; virtual concert services supplied B2B to foreign businesses fall outside Luxembourg VAT scope (reverse charge on the foreign customer), while B2C supplies of electronically supplied services to customers outside the EU are zero-rated or outside scope due to effective use and enjoyment outside the EU; B2C tickets sold to EU consumers remain taxable and are declared in Luxembourg under the OSS scheme.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic Customs Export Declaration (AES) bearing the MRN (Movement Reference Number)
Bill of Lading, CMR waybill or air waybill evidencing physical exit from EU territory
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT bank credit confirming receipt of export proceeds
Commercial invoice, virtual concert ticketing platform statement and licensing contract
Partner identification documents and proof of the foreign customer's residence (for services)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent zero-rating claims expose the SCSp and its general partner to tax fraud fines of EUR 5,000 to EUR 50,000 and imprisonment of 8 days to 3 years under Articles 1162 to 1164 of the Luxembourg VAT law; the AED may retrospectively recapture the 0% rate, impose late interest of 10% per annum, and apply penalty interest for each month of delay; insufficient transport evidence, split shipments, or failure to repatriate proceeds within the 180-day expectation automatically disallow the export exemption and trigger rectification with criminal referral in cases of intentional misdeclaration.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), operating within the Eurosystem and the European Central Bank (ECB), is the national monetary and statistical authority. Prudential and AML supervision of credit institutions is exercised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF). No separate state foreign-exchange administration exists and no exchange-control licensing authority applies.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility is guaranteed. Luxembourg applies TFEU Articles 63-66 and Directive 88/361/EEC on free movement of capital and payments; there is no approval, declaration, or surrender requirement for current-account transactions (ticket revenues, streaming royalties, platform fees) or capital-account operations (partner capital contributions, distributions). Profit remittance is unrestricted: the SCSp is fiscally transparent, so distributions follow the partnership agreement without any Luxembourg withholding tax at the partnership level. Practical gates are limited to AML/RBE source-of-funds verification, EU/OFAC sanctions screening, and BCL balance-of-payments statistical reporting by the receiving institution.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg imposes no statutory surrender timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no repatriation period for export receipts denominated in foreign currency. Obligations are statistical only: resident credit institutions report cross-border flows to BCL under Council Regulation (EC) No. 184/2005 and national BCL/CSSF reporting instructions. The SCSp may retain, convert, or disburse USD and USDC proceeds freely through the approved rails.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (EUR IBAN) and optional Capital Escrow / Formation Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Epargne de l'Etat (Spuerkeess)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and Capital Escrow / Formation Account
Operational Account; trade finance and documentary credit desk
Operational Account; FX and hedging desk

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Quintet Private Bank (Europe) S.A. (formerly KBL European Private Bankers)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Medium as a payment overlay; Low as the principal treasury rail. Legal constraints: (i) under PSD2 and the post-Brexit framework, a non-EEA EMI cannot passport into Luxembourg, so only EEA-licensed EMIs may hold or settle the SCSp's funds; (ii) substance expectations and BCL statistical reporting require the main operating IBAN to remain with a Luxembourg-resident credit institution; (iii) crypto flows via EMIs are heavily restricted unless the EMI holds a MiCAR authorisation or partners with a regulated VASP. Practical setup: use an EEA EMI (e.g., Payoneer, Airwallex, Wise Business) for ticketing-fee aggregation and refunds, sweep balances daily to the Tier 1 Luxembourg IBAN, and route all USDC through a regulated VASP-to-fiat bridge.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical attendance is effectively mandatory for new-onboarding entities: at least one natural-person manager of the general partner (or the general partner if an individual) must appear at the bank's Luxembourg office, present valid ID, execute the signature mandate (convention de signatures), and complete the in-person interview. Remote onboarding is tolerated only for existing wholesale clients using EU eIDAS qualified electronic signatures and pre-validated UBO files. Banks apply CSSF Regulation 12-02 and the amended AML Law of 12 November 2004, and will verify the SCSp's RCS registration, the RBE beneficial-ownership filing, the partnership agreement, and the source of funds for the initial deposit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp profile flagged as elevated shell-company risk: contractual partnership with no statutory minimum capital, intangible virtual-concert business, and no physical operational footprint.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised partnership agreement with capital-contribution annexes; RCS registration certificate and register of partners; RBE filing receipt; commercial substance file (Luxembourg office lease, third-party administration/substance-services agreement, manager resumes); pre-opening 12-month treasury forecast; executed commercial contracts with the ticketing platform (Stripe) and the metaverse venue operator.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Crypto-adjacent payment rail (USDC): internal suspicion that the account will aggregate digital-asset proceeds from unidentifiable counterparties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Digital-asset treasury policy (whitelisted wallets, T+1 conversion to EUR via a CSSF-supervised VASP, prohibition of unhosted-wallet counterparties); MiCAR (EU) 2023/1114 and Transfer of Funds Regulation (EU) 2023/1113 travel-rule documentation for the VASP route; sanctions-screening outputs; quarterly independent compliance attestation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident limited partners and opaque ownership cascade: pass-through structure inhibits transparency of ultimate beneficial owners.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full ownership cascade chart from each partner through to ultimate individual owners; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds certificates; accountant-certified partner financial statements where available; contractual undertaking to notify the bank of any 10% or greater partner change and to refresh the RBE filing within the legal 30-day window; powers of attorney for all mandated signatories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border USD virtual ticket sales across multiple jurisdictions: sanctions exposure, third-party intermediary risk, and chargeback/consumer-protection exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Merchant-of-record structure and platform due-diligence file (Stripe KYC/KYB); country-level geoblocking configuration for OFAC/EU-sanctioned jurisdictions; chargeback and refund policy documentation; contractual pass-through warranties with the metaverse platform; monthly transaction reconciliation of ticket sales against Stripe settlement reports.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Partner capital contributions: (i) EUR from an EU/EEA source via SEPA Credit Transfer to the SCSp's operational IBAN; (ii) non-EUR or third-country contributions via SWIFT MT103, with Field 70 referencing the capital call number and partner name and carrying the ISO 20022 purpose code 'EQUI' or the ECB Balance of Payments category 'Direct investment - equity capital'. The receiving bank verifies source of funds, applies BCL statistical tags, and performs CFSP/OFAC sanctions screening where the contributor is non-EEA. The notarial/RCS completion file (subscription schedule, signed capital call, partner identity data) must be provided before funds are released. USDC capital contributions are accepted only through the controlled VASP bridge with full on-chain transfer records and immediate fiat conversion; they are never credited directly to the IBAN.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operating payments: (i) EEA/EUR via SEPA Instant or SEPA Credit Transfer; (ii) non-EEA via SWIFT MT103 with Field 70 carrying invoice/reference data and purpose code 'SUPP' (supply/trade) or 'FEX' (professional fees); (iii) high-value licensing and metaverse-engine procurement settled by irrevocable Commercial Letters of Credit (UCP600) or standby LC confirmed by the Luxembourg bank; (iv) artist/royalty streaming via MT103 batch or EMI payout engine; (v) refunds netted within the Stripe merchant balance with a single daily EUR payout; (vi) USDC payments to blockchain-native counterparties executed exclusively from the segregated VASP wallet after counterparty KYC/AML screening and travel-rule data attachment. A monthly treasury report reconciles MT103 records, BoP coding, and the VASP ledger.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable EUR/USD forwards, typically up to 12 months, under IFEMA or ISDA 2002 master terms; no CSSF authorisation required for the SCSp as an end-user hedger.
FX swaps (spot-start reversal of USD working capital into EUR) for short-term liquidity sweeps and payment-date alignment.

Cross-currency interest rate swaps (EUR/USD CCIRS) for fixed-rate hedging of any debt tranche financing the metaverse platform build-out, subject to EMIR clearing-threshold assessment and reporting obligations.
Plain-vanilla EUR/USD options (purchased puts and calls) narrowing strike risk on large USD inflows; premium-hedging only, with the SCSp classified as an elective professional client under MiFID II.
Participating and revolving forward structures matching monthly Stripe USD batch settlements, permissible as over-the-counter hedges under the same master agreement.
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) reserved for exceptional non-deliverable currency pairs; not applicable to the core EUR/USD flow, which is fully deliverable in the EU market.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual RCS Electronic Confirmation (Confirmation électronique annuelle) of registered company data and legal representatives
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), through the eJustice portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary-based: due within one calendar month of each anniversary date of the initial RCS registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Formal reminder followed by administrative strike-off (radiation d'office) upon repeated failure; loss of legal standing and potential ex officio dissolution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of Annual Accounts (dépôt des comptes annuels) with the RCS, unless the SCSp validly applies the statutory small-entity filing exemption
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), through the eJustice portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within seven months of the financial year-end; 31 July for an SCSp with a calendar-year accounting period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fine against each defaulting general partner under Art. 2002 of the Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (generally EUR 500–25,000); court-ordered compliance and ex officio strike-off for persistent default

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership (RBE) declaration – update, reconfirmation, and correction of ultimate beneficial owner information
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE), administered by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Continuous filing obligation: update within 30 days of any limited-partner interest transfer, change of control, loss of UBO status, or material data correction; no standalone annual filing date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fines up to EUR 250,000 under the Law of 13 January 2019 as amended, imposed on general partners for intentional or negligent non-compliance; persistent default may trigger ancillary administrative strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual partnership income-tax declaration for the fiscally transparent SCSp (Luxembourg partnership tax return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) – Luxembourg direct tax administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Fiscal-year based: statutory deadline of 30 June following the calendar year, with standard e-filing extension to 31 October in administrative practice
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Formal late-filing notice, taxation d'office (third-party assessed assessment), late-payment interest, and administrative surcharge of up to 10% of the assessed tax; no direct register strike-off consequence

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent statutory audit applies if the SCSp exceeds any two of the following three criteria: balance-sheet total EUR 4.4 million, net turnover EUR 8.8 million, and average workforce of 50 employees; otherwise the SCSp qualifies as a small undertaking and is exempt from audit
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP as codified under the Law of 19 December 2002 on annual accounts, with the optional application of EU-endorsed IFRS for the undertaking's financial statements

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No standalone annual UBO form exists for the SCSp; the general partner must instead maintain a continuously accurate RBE declaration, effect updates within 30 days of any shareholding transfer or UBO change, and reconfirm beneficial ownership data as part of the RCS annual electronic confirmation procedure; a nil-change verification is recommended at each registration anniversary
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Limited Partners (parts sociales) maintained by the general partner at the partnership seat
Register of General Partner and management resolutions
Statutory minute book and written-consent records

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,500 – 3,500 per year for Luxembourg registered office and domiciliation agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 – 20,000 per year only if the statutory audit threshold is crossed; typically nil for a small or micro SCSp

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (Luxembourg City combined rate including corporate income tax of 17%, solidarity surcharge of 7% on CIT, and municipal business tax of 6.75%, applicable to profits exceeding EUR 200,000)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The SCSp is fiscally transparent; the partnership itself is not subject to Luxembourg CIT, but its partners are taxed at their own applicable rates. Qualifying partnerships may benefit from the participation exemption (100% exemption on qualifying capital gains and substantially all dividends), the patent box deduction (80% exemption of qualifying IP income, resulting in an effective CIT of approximately 5.23% on IP-derived income), and the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive regime eliminating dividend withholding tax on distributions from EU-resident subsidiaries.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (under Article 15 LIR; subject to anti-abuse rules on change of ownership)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form MDA-200 (Corporate Income Tax and Municipal Business Tax Return) filed electronically via the Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration (ACD) e-filing portal accessible through MyGuichet.lu; for fiscally transparent SCSp, the annual partnership declaration is submitted with Annex A 'Partner Allocation Schedule'
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (based on the fiscal year-end); advance CIT prepayments are generally due quarterly on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September, and 15 December
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual tax return must be filed within six months after the end of the fiscal year (i.e., 30 June for a calendar-year entity); extensions may be granted upon written request, in practice to 31 December

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: SCSp registered name, legal form, RCS Luxembourg number, LEI, fiscal reference number, and registered office address
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must identify their Luxembourg tax representative; the SCSp must indicate its transparent status and include all partner details in Annex A

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2a — Fiscal Year and Accounting Currency
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Start and end dates of the reporting period; accounting currency (EUR mandatory unless prior ACD approval is obtained)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents with a different home-country fiscal year must nonetheless report the Luxembourg fiscal period; if a functional currency is used, attach the approved concession

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profits or losses computed under Luxembourg GAAP, adjusted for transfer pricing, tax-exempt income, and non-deductible expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents must include only Luxembourg-source income attributable to a Luxembourg permanent establishment unless a DTA re-allocates the profit; attach a reconciliation to audited financial statements

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Opening loss balance, current-year offset applied, and remaining available carry-forward
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents may not offset foreign losses against Luxembourg-source income unless a DTA or the SCSp’s transparent allocation expressly allows such relief

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: For each partner: full name, residential or registered address, place of tax residence, profit-sharing percentage, and amount of profit or loss allocated
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners should provide a Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) and note any DTA claim; Luxembourg will not apply withholding tax on transparent allocations but retains reporting obligations

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing may trigger an administrative fine of up to EUR 10,000 per return, a surcharge of up to 10% of the assessed tax, and monthly late-payment interest at 0.5% from the statutory deadline; willful omission or fraudulent filing exposes the filer to criminal fines up to EUR 200,000 and imprisonment up to five years

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for profit allocations from an SCSp because the partnership is fiscally transparent and such allocations are not statutory dividends; if the SCSp were treated as opaque, the general Luxembourg corporate dividend withholding tax rate is 15%
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the beneficial owner of the income (typically the partner, not the SCSp) must submit a valid Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) issued by the home-country tax authority to the Luxembourg ACD before distribution, using the 'Relief at Source' application form through MyGuichet.lu; if tax has been withheld, a refund claim may be filed with the ACD within five years of the payment date. Under the Luxembourg DTL model, portfolio dividends are reduced to 15% and qualifying shareholdings (at least 10%) to 5%; the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive provides a 0% rate on qualifying distributions to EU corporate partners
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg does not impose statutory withholding tax on outbound interest or royalty payments, regardless of recipient residence, except in the case of certain anti-abuse or profit-distribution recharacterizations. The EU Interest & Royalties Directive reduces to 0% payments between associated enterprises of EU Member States; most Luxembourg DTA treaties provide for 0% or 5% withholding on such payments if the recipient is the beneficial owner

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local file obligation is triggered when aggregate annual cross-border related-party transactions exceed EUR 1,000,000; Master File is required where the worldwide group consolidated revenue exceeds EUR 750,000,000
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not maintain a UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime, but the ACD applies the OECD BEPS substance-over-form principle and the domestic General Anti-Abuse Rule (Article 6 OPL). An SCSp claiming treaty benefits or the participation exemption must demonstrate substance: a Luxembourg registered office, a locally resident manager or management team, physical or contractual presence, real decisions taken in Luxembourg, and substantive operational staff; a letter-box SCSp may be recharacterized as opaque, taxed at 24.94% CIT, and denied all treaty relief

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting virtual-concert ticket revenue, unreported conversion of USDC into fiat, under-declaring partner profit allocations, or falsifying the SCSp accounts
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax fraud under Article 107 LIR attracts imprisonment of up to five years and fines ranging from EUR 250,000 to EUR 500,000; administrative re-assessment at 24.94% CIT, surcharges up to 20% of tax evaded, and monthly 0.6% late interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant and any managing partner may be criminally liable; courts may pierce the corporate veil, impose civil restitution of all evaded taxes and interest, issue travel bans, freeze personal and corporate bank accounts, and disqualify the director from managing any Luxembourg entity for up to ten years

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining an SCSp with no office, no employees, no Luxembourg management meetings, no independent investment decisions, and passively routing digital ticket revenue to non-resident partners
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The ACD will apply GAAR, deny fiscal transparency, impose CIT and municipal business tax at 24.94% on the full income, and assess net wealth tax at the statutory minimum of approximately EUR 3,300; additional penalties may reach EUR 250,000
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who structured the sham vehicle face civil liability for the unpaid tax, legal reversal of the partnership's distributions, judicial liquidation, personal travel bans, and the risk of extradition for corruption where foreign clients are involved

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting USDC payments or converting cryptocurrency without performing customer due diligence, without retaining transaction records, or without registering as a virtual asset service provider if Luxembourg law determines the activity is a VASP; failing to file the RBE ultimate beneficial owner declaration
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CSSF administrative fines up to EUR 5 million or 10% of annual turnover; criminal AML penalties provide for up to five years' imprisonment and fines up to EUR 2.5 million for beneficial owners and compliance officers; the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit may freeze the SCSp's bank and crypto accounts
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly process tainted virtual-asset proceeds are personally liable for confiscation of the funds and civil damages; travel bans and precautionary seizure of personal assets may be ordered during the criminal investigation

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare or retain Master File / Local File, setting intercompany ticket-service fees or partner allocations at non-arm's-length values, or failing to file documentation within the ACD's statutory request window (typically 15 days)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Primary tax adjustment plus penalties of up to 10% per year, late-interest surcharges, and documentation fines up to EUR 100,000; intentionally false TP documentation is treated as tax evasion with criminal consequences
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The economic owner of the foreign partner entity may be deemed a de facto director; courts may reassign the income to the Luxembourg SCSp, pierce the partnership veil, and hold the director personally liable for the differential tax plus penalties and travel restrictions pending settlement

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the SCSp without timely incorporation filing in the Luxembourg Register of Commerce (RCS), without filing annual accounts, or without appointing a Luxembourg-resident manager; continuing business while the SCSp is dissolved
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Late RCS registration fines up to EUR 2,000 per month; failure to file annual accounts may result in civil dissolution, removal from the register, a fine up to EUR 10,000, and in severe cases criminal sanctions for unauthorized trading
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of a dissolved or unregistered SCSp become jointly and severally liable without benefit of the corporate veil for all debts and tax liabilities; the court may impose a personal contribution order, asset freezes, and a temporary ban on commercial activity in Luxembourg
